text: Manningham City Council acknowledges the Wurundjeri people as the traditional custodians of the land we now know as Manningham. I welcome all members of the public to this council meeting who have joined us online to observe proceedings. In response to the evolving coronavirus situation, recent changes were made to the Local Government Act which permits council meetings to be held virtually for a limited time. You won't be able to attend the meeting in person, however, you are able to watch the live meeting via our Facebook page, and you can also watch recordings of the meeting at any time that suits you. The office was unable to give us the information and ask for our contact details. No one from council contacted us for nine days and my husband had to write in on June 19th, 2020 to follow up. This is clearly not good enough. The two questions from Ms. Yee are, one, why are staff at the council's front office still not properly trained to assist ratepayers to enrol to be on the CEO's list of voters? speaker: paulmcleish

speaker: sophygalbally
text: Yeah, well, I've been on council now for about eight years, and I've been the chair of the current access and equity committee for a lot of that time. And what I've noted is that council is required to have a disability action plan. And at the moment, it's sort of immersed in the whole access and equity committee as far as our community representation is. Now, for us to have an active disability action plan, we actually have to be able to identify actions that we can actually, as a council, ensure that we're covering all the requirements for the legal requirements, that is, to provide equal access to employment, public buildings, goods and services and facilities. And that's under the Disability Discrimination Act of 1992. And for us to effectively do that, we really need to have a separate disability advisory committee. So that's the basis of my request. And the point B of part of this request is to ensure that all of our other community groups are looked after and that we actually do have focus groups. And even if it's within that same access and equity committee that's currently there. The other groups can be better represented in themselves. And that's why I've sort of asked for this report to come through and ensure that they are also respected. That's it.

speaker: paulmcleish

speaker: mikezafiropoulo

There are five or six groups. The only disadvantage is that these committees require resources to be supported and administered. However, the benefits council can get by getting proper advice, more thorough views about what is required in our community to make sure that all groups have equal chances to contribute and participate.
